Fidget toy

Manufacturing Processes/Class Project

A hand-assembled fidget toy that touches nearly every process taught in the class, from laser cutting and CNC milling to manual lathe work and injection molding.

Manufacturing Processes

Overview

The piece has an acrylic red back and a clear lever arm that were laser cut and engraved. The white block mounted to it was CNC milled, with the slots manually machined in afterward. The brass knob was manually lathed, and the feet, since lost, were injection molded. All screw holes, including those on the clear lever arm, were created using a drill press, and the toy was then assembled using the given hardware.

Fidget toy in action.

What I did

  • Laser cut and engraved the acrylic red back and the clear lever arm.
  • CNC milled the white block, then manually machined in the slots.
  • Manually lathed the brass knob.
  • Injection molded the feet (since lost).
  • Drilled all screw holes, including those on the clear lever arm, using a drill press.
  • Assembled the toy using the given hardware.
